drug_class: Anticonvulsant / Antiepileptic drug (voltage-gated sodium channel blocker)
purpose: Eslicarbazepine is used to help control partial-onset seizures in adults and children aged 4 and older with epilepsy. It is usually taken once a day, either alone or along with other seizure medications. It helps reduce how often seizures happen and makes them less severe.
how_it_works: Your brain uses electrical signals to function, but in epilepsy, those signals can become abnormal and cause seizures. Eslicarbazepine works by blocking certain channels in brain cells called sodium channels, which helps calm down those overactive electrical signals. Think of it like a circuit breaker that prevents the brain from getting overloaded and triggering a seizure.
common_side_effects: Some common side effects include dizziness, drowsiness, headache, nausea, vomiting, blurred or double vision, and feeling unsteady or uncoordinated. These effects are often mild and may improve as your body gets used to the medication. Let your doctor know if any side effects bother you.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can cause more frequent or severe seizures. Eslicarbazepine can cause low sodium levels in your blood, which may cause symptoms like headache, confusion, or swelling. It may also cause mood changes, depression, or suicidal thoughts — contact your doctor right away if this happens. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medication affects you. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding.
typical_dosing: For adults, the usual starting dose is 400 mg once daily for one to two weeks, then increased to 800 mg once daily, which is the typical maintenance dose. Some people may need up to 1,200 mg once daily depending on how well their seizures are controlled. For children, the dose is based on their weight and is determined by the doctor. Always take it at the same time each day, with or without food.
